links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of ChatGPT versus AGA patient education materials
links.effect: Mean FKGL was higher for ChatGPT than professional society materials (10.33 vs 8.72; mean difference 1.61; 95% CI 0.89–2.32; P = .00012).
links.quote: The mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was higher for ChatGPT than professional society materials (10.33 vs 8.72; mean difference, 1.61; 95% CI, 0.89–2.32; P = .00012).

links.outcome: Readability, understandability, and actionability of ChatGPT patient education versus AGA materials
links.effect: ChatGPT text was at a higher reading level (FKGL 10.33 vs 8.72), while PEMAT understandability (87.91% vs 86.52%) and actionability (78.57% vs 77.93%) did not differ significantly.
links.quote: ChatGPT-generated gastrointestinal patient education demonstrated similar quality, understandability, and actionability compared with professional society materials but was written at a significantly higher reading level.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT-generated gastrointestinal patient education materials compared to professional society materials across readability, quality, understandability, and actionability metrics, without testing a specific safeguard or deployment practice.
